KIM.thesis_one_line: Owner of grocery-anchored shopping centers with record occupancy, growing rent per share about 4% a year and paying a 5% dividend at a fair price.
kill_criteria: Pro-rata leased occupancy below 95.0% in two consecutive quarters (Q2-26: 96.4%).
Same-property NOI growth below 2.0% in two consecutive quarters (YTD "+2.6%"; outlook "+3.0% to +3.5%").
Full-year FFO per diluted share outlook midpoint cut below $1.80 (current "$1.83 to $1.84").
Consolidated net debt to annualised EBITDA above 6.5x (my basis, currently about 5.7x), or a downgrade of Moody's A3 or S&P A-.
Dividend payout above 90% of AFFO or no dividend increase in the 2027 cycle.
key_adverse_facts: 10-year Treasury about 5.2% pressures REIT multiples; stock fell from $26.38 (27 Jul 2026) to $22.44
Consolidated net debt about $8.0bn, about 5.7x annualised consolidated EBITDA (my basis), $773m of 2026 maturities to refinance
2026 net income guidance raised mainly by gains on sale, not operations
Small-shop occupancy already a record 92.9%, limiting further organic upside
June 2026 $600m 3.50% exchangeable notes (exchange price about $32.36) used partly to buy back 4.1m shares at $25.38, now above market
data_conflicts: Triage cited 26x P/E (GAAP); FFO-based P/FFO is 12.2x on the $1.835 guidance midpoint
Triage cited 6.1x leverage on an unstated basis; my consolidated net debt/EBITDA is about 5.7x (company-defined ratios not in documents opened)
Triage said about 2% forward EPS growth; company guides FFO/share +4.3% (1.835 vs 1.76) and same-property NOI +3.0% to +3.5%

CHTR.thesis_one_line: America's second-largest cable company, now merged with Cox, priced like a business in steep decline; the tiny equity slice on top of huge debt makes outcomes extreme.
kill_criteria: Charter consolidated net debt (principal) to LTM Adjusted EBITDA above 4.6x at any quarter-end (target range 4.0–4.5x, 10-K 0001091667-26-000017).
Total Internet customer net losses worse than 250k in any single quarter or worse than 500k over two consecutive quarters (Q2-26: -172k).
Combined free cash flow below $1.0bn in each of two consecutive quarters from Q4-26 (Q2-26 pre-Cox: $969m).
First 2027 capex outlook of "$11.0 billion" or more (no step-down after network evolution completes in 2027).
Permanent CFO not named by 31 Jan 2027, or any restatement or material weakness disclosure.
key_adverse_facts: Adjusted EBITDA decline accelerating: -1.2% (Q4-25), -2.2% (Q1-26), -4.3% (Q2-26); revenue -1.7%; Internet customers -172k in Q2-26 vs -116k a year earlier
Pro forma consolidated net debt about $110bn (about 4.0x my pro forma EBITDA); equity about 14% of enterprise value; new secured notes priced at 6.05% to 7.85% and exchange notes at 7.087%/7.337%
CFO Jessica Fischer resigns effective 15 Oct 2026 during Cox integration (8-K 0001140361-26-035084)
Cox revenue already falling about 4% (6M 2026 $6,067m vs $6,323m); first combined quarter not yet reported
$6.0bn Cox convertible preferred units (6.875%) and 33.6m Cox common units rank ahead of or alongside Charter common
No numeric guidance except 2026 capex about $11.4bn (excluding Cox); 2027 capex step-down, the crux of the base case, is not quantified
data_conflicts: d4/b1 market cap $13.7bn uses about 121m Class A shares; economic share count after Cox and A/N units is about 163m, i.e. about $18.4bn at $112.91
Triage 2.7x NTM P/E and 15% FCF yield are pre-Cox share-count figures; my pro forma equity FCF yield is about 27.5% (estimate)
b1 ROE 0.54 is inflated by small book equity and leverage

IVZ.thesis_one_line: Global fund manager with a big ETF business, record client inflows and rising margins, trading at about 11 times current earnings; results ride on stock-market levels.
kill_criteria: Net long-term flows negative in two consecutive quarters (Q2-26: +$45.1bn; Q1-26: +$21.8bn).
Adjusted operating margin below 32.0% in two consecutive quarters (Q2-26: 37.5%; FY25: 33.4%).
Invesco consolidated parent net debt (debt less cash) above $1.5bn (30 Jun 2026: $708.6m).
A further non-cash impairment of goodwill or intangibles above $500m (Q4-25: $1,794.9m).
Ending AUM below $2.1 trillion at any quarter-end (30 Jun 2026: $2,470bn).
key_adverse_facts: $1,794.9m non-cash impairment in Q4-25 of indefinite-lived intangibles tied to US retail mutual-fund management contracts (goodwill still $8.4bn)
Earnings levered to equity markets: Q2-26 AUM gain was mostly market (+$256.8bn) vs net long-term flows +$45.1bn; stock near 52-week high
Fundamental equities net outflow of $7.7bn in Q2-26 and net revenue yield slipping to about 22.4 bps from 23.3 bps (my calculation)
Andrew Lo, head of Asia Pacific and China JV steward, retires 31 Mar 2027 (8-K 0000914208-26-000347); he and two others sold about $7.2m of stock on 10-14 Sep 2026
$2.5bn of 5.9% MassMutual-held preferred ranks ahead of common; consolidated parent net debt $708.6m
data_conflicts: Triage cited negative ROE (-0.9%) and d4/V1 TTM GAAP net loss of $309m, caused by the one-off Q4-25 $1.795bn impairment; TTM adjusted EPS is $2.51 and return on common equity about 11.4%
Triage said forward-earnings data missing; d4 has FY26 EPS $2.81 and FY27 $3.26
V1 verdict label 'excessive' rests on TTM GAAP ROE of -2.5%; on adjusted earnings the stock is priced for about the ROE it earns
IVZ.next_earnings_date_basis: estimated from prior-year cadence (Q3-25 released 2025-10-28); not announced in filings reviewed
IVZ.confidence_in_thesis: medium: record flows and margins are filed facts, but the earnings base is market-cyclical and Q2 was flattered by a market rally

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1 compares the P/B-implied ROE of 11.3% with TTM GAAP ROE of -2.5%, which includes the one-off $1.795bn impairment; on TTM adjusted earnings of $1,139m over about $10.0bn of common equity ROE is about 11.4%, so the price is roughly fair, not excessive. Base returns agree (mine +8.0% vs V1 +6.9%). Reverse DCF implies about 2.5% 10-year FCF growth versus my base of about 6.7%.

IVZ.scenario_basis: Start adjusted EPS $2.84 (Q2-26 x4; TTM $2.51); 2029 adjusted EPS $2.15/$3.45/$4.15, exit P/E 8.5x/10.5x/12.0x, dividend $0.86 growing 5% (cumulative about $2.7); start price $30.92
